q: Hazzard describes increasing difficulty focusing on near targets beginning around age 45. Which mechanism accounts for this age-related loss of accommodation?
o: Reduced pupil size and reduced light transmission impair near accommodation.
Reduced lens flexibility and reduced ciliary muscle tone impair near accommodation.
Macular degeneration and loss of central retinal fixation impair near accommodation.
Peripheral visual-field loss and reduced obstacle detection impair near accommodation.
explanation:
Presbyopia is the age-related decline in the ability to focus on a near target. **Reduced lens flexibility and changes in the ciliary apparatus impair accommodation.**

**A. Reduced pupil size and reduced light transmission impair near accommodation.** Smaller pupils reduce incoming light, but do not explain the loss of lens shape change.
**B. Reduced lens flexibility and reduced ciliary muscle tone impair near accommodation.** Accommodation requires the lens to change curvature. Aging makes it less able to do so.
**C. Macular degeneration and loss of central retinal fixation impair near accommodation.** Macular damage impairs central vision without being the mechanism of presbyopia.
**D. Peripheral visual-field loss and reduced obstacle detection impair near accommodation.** Peripheral field loss affects obstacle detection rather than near focusing power.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 471.
label: Source: hazzard marked .pdf · 471, Table 33-1

optionRationales.body: . Reduced pupil size and reduced light transmission impair near accommodation.** Smaller pupils reduce incoming light, but do not explain the loss of lens shape change.
. Reduced lens flexibility and reduced ciliary muscle tone impair near accommodation.** Accommodation requires the lens to change curvature. Aging makes it less able to do so.
. Macular degeneration and loss of central retinal fixation impair near accommodation.** Macular damage impairs central vision without being the mechanism of presbyopia.
. Peripheral visual-field loss and reduced obstacle detection impair near accommodation.** Peripheral field loss affects obstacle detection rather than near focusing power.

explanationParts.text: Presbyopia is the age-related decline in the ability to focus on a near target. **Reduced lens flexibility and changes in the ciliary apparatus impair accommodation.**

q: רופא מדווח למרב״ד על מצב רפואי קבוע העלול לסכן נהיגה. איזה תיאור של משמעות הדיווח נכון לפי החוזר?
o: הדיווח קובע פסילה מיידית של הרישיון ללא הערכה נוספת
הדיווח מפנה לבדיקה לצורך המלצה על הגבלות נהיגה
הדיווח מעביר לרופא המטפל סמכות להנפיק רישיון מוגבל
הדיווח מחייב חזרה לנהיגה רגילה אם הראייה נמצאה תקינה
explanation:
הודעה רפואית למרב״ד מפנה את הנהג להערכת כשירות. הגבלות רישוי נקבעות לאחר הבדיקה ובהחלטת רשות הרישוי. **הדיווח מפנה לבדיקה לצורך המלצה על הגבלות נהיגה**.

**א. הדיווח קובע פסילה מיידית של הרישיון ללא הערכה נוספת.** הדיווח כשלעצמו אינו פוסל מיידית.
**ב. הדיווח מפנה לבדיקה לצורך המלצה על הגבלות נהיגה.** המרב״ד עשוי להמליץ על הגבלות או התאמות מתאימות.
**ג. הדיווח מעביר לרופא המטפל סמכות להנפיק רישיון מוגבל.** הרופא המטפל אינו מנפיק רישיון מכוח הדיווח.
**ד. הדיווח מחייב חזרה לנהיגה רגילה אם הראייה נמצאה תקינה.** ראייה היא רק אחד המרכיבים בכשירות לנהיגה.

q: After complete NSCLC resection with pathologic N2 involvement, which result of LungART most affects the decision about routine postoperative radiotherapy?
o: A survival gain concentrated among patients over age 75
Additional cardiopulmonary toxicity without a demonstrated survival gain
A reduction in distant metastases sufficient to avoid systemic treatment
A fall in both pulmonary complications and nodal recurrence
explanation:
**A.** The trial did not establish an age-specific survival gain for routine postoperative radiation.
**B.** The trial did not establish a survival advantage from routine postoperative radiation and reported additional cardiopulmonary toxicity. Locoregional control alone cannot be equated with improved survival.
**C.** Regional radiation does not substitute for systemic treatment of occult distant disease.
**D.** The cardiopulmonary toxicity signal points in the opposite direction.

optionRationales.body: .** The trial did not establish an age-specific survival gain for routine postoperative radiation.

.** The trial did not establish a survival advantage from routine postoperative radiation and reported additional cardiopulmonary toxicity. Locoregional control alone cannot be equated with improved survival.
.** Regional radiation does not substitute for systemic treatment of occult distant disease.
.** The cardiopulmonary toxicity signal points in the opposite direction.

q: בן 80 עם סרטן לבלב גרורתי שוקל ERCP להקלה על חסימה. הוא מסוגל להחליט ואומר שברצונו לבלות זמן עם נכדיו; אשתו מדגישה הימנעות מאשפוז. לפני המלצה משותפת, איזה צעד שומר על בחירה מדעת של המטופל?
o: להציג את סיכויי ההצלחה הטכנית כבסיס לבחירה.
לברר העדפות ולדון בתועלת, בסיכונים ובחלופות.
לבקש מאשתו לבחור לפי אפשרות השהייה בבית.
לבסס את ההמלצה על תוספת ההישרדות המשוערת.
explanation:
בהחלטה משותפת מחברים בין נתוני התועלת והסיכון לבין התוצאות שהמטופל עצמו מייחס להן חשיבות. **לברר את העדפותיו ולהסביר תועלת, סיכונים וחלופות**.

**א. להציג את סיכויי ההצלחה הטכנית כבסיס לבחירה** — הצלחה טכנית אינה בהכרח תוצאה רצויה מבחינת האדם.
**ב. לברר העדפות ולדון בתועלת, בסיכונים ובחלופות** — בירור ערכים והסבר החלופות מאפשרים בחירה מדעת.
**ג. לבקש מאשתו לבחור לפי אפשרות השהייה בבית** — עמדת בת הזוג עשויה להיות חשובה לתכנון ואינה מחליפה את העדפת המטופל.
**ד. לבסס את ההמלצה על תוספת ההישרדות המשוערת** — תוחלת חיים היא שיקול אחד לצד תפקוד, עומס הטיפול ואיכות החיים.

אסמכתא · חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 עמ׳ 8.

q: An 81-year-old man with advanced COPD has refractory dyspnea despite optimal treatment of the underlying disease. An opioid is being considered for palliation. Which potential benefit and cognitive risk are described by Hazzard?
o: Relief of breathlessness with possible impaired alertness.
Improved oxygenation through recruitment of collapsed alveoli.
Improved ventilation through increased respiratory muscle strength.
Lower pulmonary vascular pressure with improved right-heart output.
explanation:
An opioid may reduce the sensation of otherwise refractory breathlessness. **Potential relief must be balanced against reduced mental functioning**, especially when alertness matters to the patient.

**A. Relief of breathlessness with possible impaired alertness** — An opioid can reduce the perception of otherwise refractory dyspnea but can also reduce alertness or mental functioning. Titrate to distress and adverse effects.
**B. Improved oxygenation through recruitment of collapsed alveoli** — Opioids do not recruit collapsed alveoli as a mechanism for relief of breathlessness.
**C. Improved ventilation through increased respiratory muscle strength** — They do not restore respiratory muscle strength.
**D. Lower pulmonary vascular pressure with improved right-heart output** — Relief of dyspnea does not require a direct reduction in pulmonary vascular pressure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

. Improved ventilation through increased respiratory muscle strength** — They do not restore respiratory muscle strength.
. Lower pulmonary vascular pressure with improved right-heart output** — Relief of dyspnea does not require a direct reduction in pulmonary vascular pressure.

q: A patient receiving antiresorptive treatment underwent a tooth extraction. An area of exposed, necrotic jaw bone has now failed to heal for ten weeks. Which complication matches this finding?
o: An atypical insufficiency fracture of the femur during antiresorptive treatment
Reduced bone density measured during the course of antiresorptive treatment
Osteonecrosis of the jaw associated with antiresorptive treatment
Joint pain without bone damage following the use of antiresorptive treatment
explanation:
Osteonecrosis of the jaw can present as an extraction site where bone remains exposed and fails to heal. **Ten weeks of exposed necrotic jaw bone during antiresorptive treatment fits this complication.**

**A. Atypical femoral fracture** This injury affects the subtrochanteric femur or shaft and commonly presents with thigh or groin pain.
**B. Reduced bone density** A DXA measurement describes bone mass. It does not explain visible necrotic bone in the mouth.
**C. Osteonecrosis of the jaw** The eight-week persistence criterion is met. Dental extraction is a recognized precipitating event.
**D. Joint pain** Arthralgia can cause discomfort but does not cause an exposed, nonhealing area of jaw bone.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 777, osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fractures.

. Reduced bone density** A DXA measurement describes bone mass. It does not explain visible necrotic bone in the mouth.
. Osteonecrosis of the jaw** The eight-week persistence criterion is met. Dental extraction is a recognized precipitating event.
. Joint pain** Arthralgia can cause discomfort but does not cause an exposed, nonhealing area of jaw bone.

q: For a basal cell carcinoma located in a low-risk area, which combination of life expectancy and additional lesion risk does Hazzard describe for discussing active surveillance?
o: Prolonged life expectancy and a lesion with additional risk factors
Limited life expectancy and a lesion without additional risk factors
Limited life expectancy and a lesion with additional risk factors
Prolonged life expectancy and a lesion without additional risk factors
explanation:
Active surveillance can suit a slow-growing BCC when treatment burden exceeds likely benefit within the patient's lifetime. **Limited life expectancy and no additional lesion risk factors** fit the scenario best.

**A. Long expectancy with risk factors.** Both time for progression and lesion risk argue for closer consideration of active treatment.
**B. Limited expectancy, low-risk lesion.** Monitor for growth and symptoms, with the option to treat if burdens develop.
**C. Limited expectancy with risk factors.** High-risk features can shorten the time to clinically important local injury.
**D. Long expectancy, low-risk lesion.** A longer horizon gives even a slowly growing lesion more time to cause problems.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1463.

. Limited expectancy, low-risk lesion.** Monitor for growth and symptoms, with the option to treat if burdens develop.
. Limited expectancy with risk factors.** High-risk features can shorten the time to clinically important local injury.
. Long expectancy, low-risk lesion.** A longer horizon gives even a slowly growing lesion more time to cause problems.

q: A 72-year-old man with obesity (BMI 38), fatigue, reduced libido, and a total testosterone level of 8.5 nmol/L sleeps poorly and snores. Which approach is supported before considering testosterone treatment?
o: Begin testosterone replacement and postpone evaluation of the suspected sleep disorder
Arrange sleep testing and encourage weight reduction while evaluating the testosterone deficiency
Treat the low testosterone as irreversible and prioritize replacement over evaluating underlying causes
Use DHEA replacement and postpone evaluation of the suspected sleep disorder
explanation:
Obesity can contribute to reversible testosterone suppression, and snoring with disturbed sleep raises suspicion for obstructive sleep apnea. **Arrange sleep testing, support weight reduction and confirm the low testosterone with a repeat morning measurement before considering replacement.**

**A. Start testosterone now** — One low result is insufficient. Untreated severe obstructive sleep apnea is a reason to defer testosterone therapy.
**B. Sleep testing and weight reduction** — Sleep testing addresses the snoring and fatigue. Evaluate obesity and other reversible contributors while confirming whether he has symptomatic androgen deficiency.
**C. Assume irreversible deficiency** — Functional suppression can improve when its cause is addressed. This presentation has not shown permanent testicular or pituitary failure.
**D. Use DHEA first** — Giving an androgen precursor neither evaluates the suspected sleep disorder nor confirms or treats the underlying cause of the low result.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 552, 647, 1534 (Table 97-5). Endocrine Society, Testosterone Therapy in Men With Hypogonadism, recommendation 2.2.
ref: Hazzard Ch 37 — SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN
chapterTitle: SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN

q: בן 80, ברקע סרטן ראות מסוג Small-Cell Lung Carcinoma (SCLC). מספר חודשים סובל מחולשה פרוקסימלית של הידיים והרגליים, קושי להרים ידיים מעל הראש ולעמוד מישיבה, והיפו-רפלקסיה. מה יחזק את האבחנה המשוערת?
o: בבדיקת דם נוגדנים נגד רצפטורי אצטילכולין
חזר לאחרונה מטיול למזרח הרחוק עם אכילה בשווקים
Exophthalmos ו- TSH נמוך
למטופל יש אורטוסטטיזם ופה יבש
explanation:
Small-cell lung cancer, proximal weakness and depressed reflexes suggest Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome, a presynaptic neuromuscular disorder. **Orthostatic symptoms and dry mouth** strengthen the diagnosis through evidence of autonomic involvement.

**A. Acetylcholine-receptor antibodies.** These point toward postsynaptic myasthenia gravis rather than Lambert–Eaton syndrome.
**B. Recent travel and food exposure.** An acute foodborne paralytic illness would have a different time course from months of proximal weakness.
**C. Exophthalmos and low TSH.** These suggest Graves hyperthyroidism, which does not explain the characteristic combination of hyporeflexia and autonomic symptoms.
**D. Orthostasis and dry mouth.** Autonomic dysfunction commonly accompanies the weakness and reflex changes in Lambert–Eaton syndrome.

Reference · Ivanovski and Miralles, Degenerative Neurological and Neuromuscular Disease 2019, pp. 9–27. Hazzard 8e, p. 1626.
